text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers onThursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Experience of negotiating with Moscow will help in dealing with Washington, parliament head Vytautas Landsbergis said after meeting U.S. vice-president Al Gore.
- Police cannot find Valdemaras Butenas, former head of Ukio Bank, to interrogate him as a witness on dubious loans.
- A German interior ministry delegation to investigate the possibility of starting a visa-free regime countries will arrive in June instead of March.
- The government decided on Wednesday to increase the minimum salary to 400 litas from 330 litas.
- The textile industry exported goods worth two billion litas in 1996, 15.2 percent of total exports.
- Parliament decided to limit strictly tobacco and alcohol advertising instead of banning it.
- A $40 million bond issue by Mazeikiu Nafta distributed via Credit Suisse First Boston in February was acquired by Union Bank of Switzerland, newspaper sources said.
- The government decided on Wednesday to increase excise duties on alcohol, tobacco and petroleum to pay higher salaries in the health care sector.
- People thought that 1994 saw the end of the notorious crime gangs the Vilnius brigade and Pantera Mafia but the same mobsters are making attempts to regain their influence.

- Danish Odense Staalskibsvaerst acquired a stake of 43.65 percent in Baltija Ship Yard for over 15 million litas, newspaper sources say. The newspaper also said the Danes intend to invest $10 million into the company.
- The U.S. will not leave Lithuania in a "grey zone", Gore told Landsbergis in Washington.
